title: The Column Law and Torsion in Chessboard Complexes
content: We study the joint kernel of operators that replace an ordinary tensor factor by an odd marker. In characteristic zero its decomposition deletes the first column of each site partition. Over every field, ballot words describe the leading words of every socle layer and give dimensions independent of the characteristic. The closed cochains form a free associative algebra generated by prime ballot words; we determine its hook-shaped generator multiplicities. A Grassmannian evaluation map gives exact polynomial-exponential growth below the free range. A cyclic frame reduces group-invariant closure to one equation. The Cartan complex identifies exterior-algebra Ext with the homology of row-bounded rook complexes. Their top cycles have field-independent dimension, so the next integral homology group is torsion-free. For rectangular chessboards this proves the torsion-free half of a conjecture of Shareshian and Wachs on higher chessboard homology and, together with known torsion results, completes their criterion for torsion in bottom homology.
